plan.title: 4 Variations of the Indian Head Nod
plan.summary: A lighthearted travel reel demonstrating four distinct variations of the Indian head nod from a bustling street, intercut with real-life clips of locals doing each gesture.

shots.title: Intro in the Market
shots.purpose: hook: introduce the cultural observation in a lively setting, curious and friendly
shots.scene: Stand in a busy outdoor market street.

framing.note: Center yourself from the waist up with a busy street behind you.

pose.description: Standing upright facing the camera, then turning slightly to the side while gesturing.

steps.instruction: Stand facing the camera in a busy street and introduce your topic.
Turn slightly to your side and gesture casually with your hand as you finish the sentence.

script.text: While traveling around India, I've noticed four variations of the head nod, and it is a gesture of agreeance.

shots.title: Demonstrating Variation 1
shots.purpose: setup: demonstrate the first variation, playful and clear
shots.scene: Stand in the same busy outdoor street.

framing.note: Keep yourself centered from the waist up so your head movement is clear.

pose.description: Facing forward, tilting head side to side with a warm smile.

steps.instruction: Look straight into the lens and announce the first variation.
Smile and gently tilt your head from side to side.

script.text: So the first one is like this.

shots.title: Real Examples of Variation 1
shots.purpose: reveal: real-life examples of the first head nod, warm and authentic
shots.scene: At street stalls and walkways with locals.

framing.note: Frame the people you interact with from the waist up.

pose.description: People sitting or standing in shops and streets tilting their heads in agreement.

steps.instruction: Film four quick clips of people smiling and giving a slow side-to-side head tilt as you chat or hand them something.

shots.title: Demonstrating Variation 2
shots.purpose: setup: introduce and demonstrate the second variation, upbeat
shots.scene: Stand in the busy outdoor street.

framing.note: Frame yourself from the waist up, centered.

pose.description: Standing straight and giving a quick single side tilt of the head.

steps.instruction: Say your line, then immediately do one fast side-to-side head waggle.

shots.title: Real Examples of Variation 2
shots.purpose: reveal: real-life clips of the quick nod, lively and candid
shots.scene: Along the street and inside local shops.

framing.note: Keep each person centered from the chest or waist up.

pose.description: People on the street and behind shop counters giving a quick head tilt.

steps.instruction: Film three quick clips of people passing by or behind shop counters giving a fast, friendly head tilt.

shots.title: Demonstrating Variation 3
shots.purpose: setup: show the third variation, energetic
shots.scene: Stand in the busy market street.

framing.note: Center yourself from the waist up.

pose.description: Facing camera and shaking head rapidly side to side with a slight tilt.

steps.instruction: Introduce the third nod, then wiggle your head quickly from side to side.

shots.title: Real Examples of Variation 3
shots.purpose: reveal: show locals doing the rapid head waggle, cheerful
shots.scene: Inside a clothing shop and a lobby.

framing.note: Frame the subject from the waist up.

pose.description: Standing indoors, smiling and waggling head rapidly in agreement.

steps.instruction: Record two short clips of people indoors smiling and giving a continuous, rapid head waggle.

shots.title: Explanation & Variation 4 Demo
shots.purpose: setup: explain the confusion and demonstrate the fourth variation, relatable and expressive
shots.scene: Stand in the busy outdoor street.

framing.note: Center yourself from the waist up with room for hand gestures.

pose.description: Speaking with open hands, then tilting head down and to the side.

steps.instruction: Explain how the gesture used to confuse you while gesturing with both hands open.
Introduce the last variation, then dip your head down and to the side with a smile.

script.text: And I used to get very confused cause it almost looks like they're saying no, but they're actually just agreeing with you.

shots.title: Real Example of Variation 4
shots.purpose: reveal: show a real example of the fourth nod, charming
shots.scene: Inside a bright shop with a friend holding a mini mic.

framing.note: Frame the person from the waist up.

pose.description: Man in a shop dipping his head to the side while smiling.

steps.instruction: Film a clip of someone smiling and dipping their head to the side in agreement during an interview.

shots.title: Outro in the Market
shots.purpose: payoff: wrap up with a sweet personal takeaway while doing the nod yourself, endearing
shots.scene: Stand in the busy outdoor street.

framing.note: Center yourself from the waist up.

pose.description: Smiling warmly at the camera with hands clasped in front while doing the head nod.

steps.instruction: Smile warmly, bring your hands together in front of you, and do the side-to-side head nod as you say your final line.

script.text: And I find it so cute, I have even started to do it.

plan.title: Unboxing a New Eilik Robot Companion
plan.summary: Unbox a new desktop robot toy alongside your first one, power it on, and pet its head to turn a grumpy face into a happy dance.

shots.title: The New Arrival
shots.purpose: hook: introduce the new arrival and spark curiosity
shots.scene: On the floor against a wall with your first robot toy.

framing.note: Keep the first toy on the right, then pan left as the new box lands.

pose.description: No person in frame; just a hand placing the box down.

steps.instruction: Start on your first robot toy with the caption 'A new Eilik is here!' on screen.
Pan left and set the new box down next to it.

shots.title: Surprised Reaction
shots.purpose: setup: show the first toy's surprised reaction
shots.scene: Close to the floor right in front of the robot and box.

framing.note: Frame the robot on the right looking at the box on the left.

pose.description: No person in frame.

steps.instruction: Film your robot looking at the box and place a surprised emoji above its head.

shots.title: Knocking on the Box
shots.purpose: setup: build anticipation with a cute interaction
shots.scene: On the floor angled toward the front of the box.

framing.note: Angle from the side so the robot's arm touches the box.

pose.description: No person in frame.

steps.instruction: Capture the robot tapping its arm against the box with the text '*knocks*' on screen.

shots.title: Heart Eyes
shots.purpose: setup: show excitement for the new friend inside
shots.scene: On the floor facing the robot.

framing.note: Center on the robot's face showing heart eyes.

pose.description: No person in frame.

steps.instruction: Slowly push in on the robot's heart-eyes screen with a heart-eyes emoji above it.

shots.title: Sliding Off the Sleeve
shots.purpose: setup: begin the unboxing
shots.scene: On the floor in front of the packaged box.

framing.note: Center the box in frame with room above to slide the sleeve off.

pose.description: Two hands at the top of the frame lifting the box sleeve.

steps.instruction: Show the caption 'Let's unbox her!' and slide the outer sleeve straight up off the box.

shots.title: Opening the Cardboard Box
shots.purpose: setup: continue the unboxing build-up
shots.scene: On the floor beside the inner cardboard box.

framing.note: Angle slightly from the side to show the box lid opening.

pose.description: A hand lifting the cardboard flap.

steps.instruction: Keep the caption up and lift the cardboard lid open with one hand.

shots.title: First Peek Inside
shots.purpose: reveal: first peek at the new toy inside the box
shots.scene: Above the open box on the floor.

framing.note: Look down into the open box to show the toy inside.

pose.description: No person in frame.

steps.instruction: Point the camera down into the open box and add the caption 'Wow! 😆'.

shots.title: Removing the Plastic Shell
shots.purpose: reveal: free the toy from its packaging
shots.scene: On the floor in front of the plastic casing.

framing.note: Center the plastic shell on the floor.

pose.description: Hands pulling the two halves of the plastic shell apart.

steps.instruction: Set the plastic case on the floor and pull the top cover apart with both hands.

shots.title: Powering On
shots.purpose: reveal: bring the new toy to life and show its expressions
shots.scene: On the floor facing the new robot.

framing.note: Center the new robot upright on its stand.

pose.description: A thumb pressing the button on the robot's chest.

steps.instruction: Show the caption 'Let's power her on!' and press and hold the button on the toy's chest.
Move your hand away and let the camera capture its startup animations.

shots.title: Grumpy Face Close-Up
shots.purpose: setup: highlight a funny grumpy expression
shots.scene: Right in front of the robot's face.

framing.note: Tight close-up on the robot's face and grumpy eyes.

pose.description: No person in frame.

steps.instruction: Zoom in close on the angry eyes and add the text 'Why is she so angry?'.

shots.title: Making Her Happy
shots.purpose: payoff: cheer the robot up for a sweet, happy ending
shots.scene: On the floor facing the robot.

framing.note: Center the robot with room above for your hand to pet its head.

pose.description: A hand gently patting the top of the robot's head.

steps.instruction: Show the text 'Let's make her happy!' and gently pet the top of the robot's head.
Switch the text to a smiley emoji as the robot starts smiling and dancing.
Take your hand away and finish with the caption 'Thanks for watching!'.

plan.title: 3-Ingredient No-Oven Oreo Cake
plan.summary: A fast-paced, no-oven recipe tutorial showing how to make a 3-ingredient Oreo cake in the microwave, starting with a mouthwatering fork-bite hook and ending with a glossy chocolate ganache pour.

shots.title: The Fork Bite Hook
shots.purpose: hook: mouthwatering close-up of the finished cake being cut to grab attention immediately
shots.scene: At a kitchen counter or table with the finished cake on parchment paper.

framing.note: Close-up of the slice of cake in the foreground with the rest of the cake and cookie packages behind it.

pose.description: No full person in frame; just a hand entering from the top with a fork.

steps.instruction: Press record with the camera pointing down at the slice of cake, and press a fork down through the tip of the slice.
Lift the bite of cake on the fork up toward the lens so the texture shows clearly.

script.text: I am so shocked at how good this cake is.
It's only three ingredients and you don't even need an oven.

shots.title: Separate and Crush Cookies
shots.purpose: setup: fast-paced preparation of the main cookie ingredient
shots.scene: Overhead view of your kitchen counter with two bowls and a zip-top bag.

framing.note: Overhead view of a large glass bowl and a small white bowl on a wooden counter.

pose.description: Hands working over the bowls from the bottom of the frame.

steps.instruction: Hold two packs of sandwich cookies over the bowls, then drop them in.
Scrape the white cream filling off a cookie with a knife into the small bowl and drop the cookie half into the large bowl.
Put the cookies in a zip-top bag and roll a rolling pin over them to crush them.
Pour the crushed cookie crumbs from the bag into the large glass bowl.

script.text: All you need to do is separate the Oreo biscuit and filling,

shots.title: Mix the Batter
shots.purpose: setup: showing how quickly the batter comes together in one bowl
shots.scene: Directly above the glass mixing bowl on the counter.

framing.note: Centered overhead shot of the glass mixing bowl filling most of the middle of the frame.

pose.description: Hands pouring ingredients and whisking in the bowl.

steps.instruction: Tip a teaspoon of baking powder into the bowl of cookie crumbs and whisk them together.
Pour a jug of milk into the center of the crumbs.
Scrape the reserved cookie filling from the small bowl into the mix.
Whisk the batter until it looks dark and smooth.

script.text: Add baking powder and mix these together,
then pour in milk and add the Oreo filling
and stir everything together until smooth.

shots.title: Prep Mould and Microwave
shots.purpose: setup: prepping the pan and cooking the cake without an oven
shots.scene: At the counter with a microwave-safe round cake mould.

framing.note: Angled close-up of the round cake mould centered on the counter.

pose.description: Hands prepping the mould and pouring batter.

steps.instruction: Brush the inside of your microwave-safe cake mould with oil.
Press a circle of parchment paper flat into the bottom of the mould.
Pour the smooth cookie batter into the mould.
Pick up the filled mould with both hands and lift it out of the frame, leaving the empty counter to add your cooking time text.

script.text: Now grease and line a microwaveable cake mould or something similar,
and microwave for about six minutes.

shots.title: Unmould the Cake
shots.purpose: reveal: unmoulding the cooked cake cleanly
shots.scene: At the counter with a wire cooling rack over parchment paper.

framing.note: Close-up of the cake on a wire cooling rack placed over parchment paper.

pose.description: Hands lifting the mould and peeling paper off the cake.

steps.instruction: Lift the cake mould straight up off the cooling rack to reveal the cooked cake.
Peel the circle of parchment paper gently off the top of the cake.

script.text: Let it cool fully, then turn it upside down.

shots.title: Pour Ganache and Garnish
shots.purpose: payoff: glossy chocolate pour and garnish for a bakery-style finish
shots.scene: At the counter with the cooled cake on the wire rack.

framing.note: Close-up of the round cake on the wire rack, filling the center of the frame.

pose.description: Hand pouring chocolate ganache, spreading it with a spoon, and sprinkling crumbs.

steps.instruction: Pour glossy melted chocolate ganache right into the center of the cake.
Swirl the back of a spoon in circles over the top to spread the chocolate to the edges.
Sprinkle a pinch of reserved cookie crumbs around the outer edge of the cake to finish.

script.text: You can eat it like this or add a topping to make it look and taste even better.

plan.title: 3 Creative Phone Camera Transitions: BTS vs Result
plan.summary: A behind-the-scenes vs. final result short showing three creative camera moves filmed on a phone—a bus window push-in, a roadside car whip-pan, and a cycling tilt-down—followed by the seamlessly edited results.

shots.title: BTS Bus Window
shots.purpose: hook: behind-the-scenes setup, curious
shots.scene: Sit in a bus or train seat next to a window with a decal.

framing.note: Medium shot from a high angle showing the person sitting by a window.

pose.description: Sitting in a seat, holding a phone toward the window.

steps.instruction: Have a friend film you from above as you push your phone slowly toward the window.

shots.title: BTS Roadside Car Pass
shots.purpose: setup: behind-the-scenes action, energetic
shots.scene: Stand safely on the edge of a tree-lined road.

framing.note: Wide shot showing two people on the roadside as a car passes.

pose.description: Crouching by the road, swinging phone to follow a passing car.

steps.instruction: Hold your phone out toward the road as a car approaches.
Swing your arm quickly to follow the car as it drives past, finishing by pointing up at the trees.

shots.title: BTS Cycling
shots.purpose: setup: behind-the-scenes action, dynamic
shots.scene: Ride a bicycle along a tree-lined path with friends.

framing.note: Wide shot from behind cyclists riding on a path.

pose.description: Riding a bicycle while holding a phone up in one hand.

steps.instruction: Ride your bike while holding your phone high up, then lower it down in front of you.

shots.title: Result: Window Reveal
shots.purpose: reveal: the resulting cinematic shot from the bus, smooth
shots.scene: Inside a moving vehicle looking out a window with a hole in the decal over a bridge.

framing.note: Wide view looking out the window at a bridge and water.

pose.description: No person in shot; camera moves through window frame.

steps.instruction: Push the phone smoothly forward through the clear circle on the window to reveal the view outside.

shots.title: Result: Car Whip Pan
shots.purpose: payoff: the resulting dynamic car transition, exciting
shots.scene: On the side of a tree-lined road as a car drives by.

framing.note: Wide shot of a car driving past on a road under trees.

pose.description: No person in shot; tracking a passing car.

steps.instruction: Tilt down from the trees to frame the approaching car.
Pan fast right across the side of the car as it passes closely, then tilt straight up into the trees.

shots.title: Result: Cycling Reveal
shots.purpose: payoff: final seamless transition to the cycling shot, carefree
shots.scene: Riding on a path behind friends on bicycles.

framing.note: Wide shot following cyclists riding away on a path.

pose.description: Cyclists riding away from the camera.

steps.instruction: Tilt down from the sky and trees to reveal your friends riding their bikes ahead of you.

plan.title: Two Choices Motivational Walk
plan.summary: A moody, slow-motion motivational video following someone walking down a misty path through tall grass while a four-part quote about choices appears on screen to dramatic music.

shots.title: Misty Path Walk with Quote
shots.purpose: hook and payoff: moody, reflective setup that builds to a determined motivational message
shots.scene: On a narrow path through tall grass near trees on a misty day

framing.note: Wide shot with the person centered in the lower middle of the frame, surrounded by tall grass and trees in the background.

pose.description: Walking slowly away from the camera with back turned, hands relaxed at sides.

steps.instruction: Walk slowly behind your subject down the path while showing the first line of your quote on screen.
Keep moving forward smoothly at the same pace and update the text to the second line.
Continue walking forward through the grass and display the third line of text.
Keep following steadily behind your subject and show the final line of your quote until the end.

plan.title: Upbeat Partner Dance Routine
plan.summary: A single-take, full-body partner dance routine set to an upbeat Indian song in a studio.

shots.title: Full Partner Dance Routine
shots.purpose: hook and payoff: playful, energetic partner dance routine from start to finish.
shots.scene: In a dance studio or open room with a wooden floor and plain wall.

framing.note: Full-body shot of two people standing side by side with room to move.

pose.description: Standing side-by-side, one partner resting an arm on the other's shoulder while the other crosses their arms.

steps.instruction: Stand side-by-side; have one partner rest an arm on the other's shoulder while looking at each other playfully.
Step apart slightly and sway forward and back with light hand gestures to the vocal melody.
Groove in place, tapping your feet and swaying your hips to the rhythm.
Break into the main upbeat chorus choreography, raising your hands near your head and stepping side to side.
Turn toward each other and perform playful, synchronized hand waves and footwork.
Repeat the energetic chorus steps, sweeping your arms and bouncing to the beat.
Face each other again with expressive hand gestures around the face and quick steps.
Slide sideways together across the floor while grooving and smiling to finish the routine.
